transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I can’t keep my thoughts and words in a straight line anymore. I’ll start talking about an overnight shift, then somehow I’m on soccer, paint colors, patient charts... and people look confused. I can tell I’m losing them.
Over the past week or two, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual and needing very little sleep?
No, I haven’t really noticed feeling especially up or energized. I’m not sure about the sleep part—I don’t think I’ve been needing a lot less than usual.
Have you noticed anything unusual like hearing voices others don't hear, or having beliefs that others say aren't true, and if so, how long has that been going on?

I don’t hear voices, but I’m sure my supervisors changed my shifts on purpose and watch me through the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe. People keep saying it’s just staffing shortages, but I don’t believe that.
How long have you been noticing these beliefs about being watched and having your shifts changed on purpose—has it been going on for a few weeks, or more like several months or longer?
It’s been going on for about a year now—maybe a year and a month. The watching and the way I’ve been acting, getting scattered like that.
Have you been using any drugs, alcohol, or new medications, or do you have any medical conditions that started around the same time as these symptoms?
I’m not really sure what would count. I haven’t noticed anything starting around then that I can point to.
Over this past year, has your ability to perform your job duties or maintain your relationships changed compared to before these beliefs and disorganized thinking started?

Yeah. At work I’ve needed coworkers to double-check my rounds and my charting. At home, I’m behind on bills, I’ve ignored my friends, and my apartment’s gotten really out of control. It got bad enough that employee health sent me for an emergency evaluation after I told them I’d been thinking about suicide.
Over this past year, have you also been experiencing periods of feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, separate from the suicidal thoughts you mentioned?
Yeah. Most days I wake up feeling really heavy and empty. After work, sometimes I just sit in my car and cry for a while before I can make myself drive home.

Thinking back over this past year, have there been stretches of time—say, two weeks or more—when you still had these beliefs about being watched or the disorganized thinking, but you were NOT feeling depressed, empty, or tearful?
Yeah. There were a few weeks where I wasn’t in that really deep depressed place, but I still thought the cameras and supervisors were monitoring me. I was still really guarded at work.

Over this past year, would you say the depressed, empty feelings have been present most of the time alongside the paranoid beliefs, or have they come and gone, with more weeks where you felt okay mood-wise?
I’d say it’s been there most of the time. Even when the camera stuff or my thoughts weren’t as bad, I still felt heavy and empty, and didn’t really care about things.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has over a year of persistent psychotic symptoms (paranoid delusions about surveillance, disorganized speech/thought) meeting Criterion A duration for schizophrenia-spectrum illness. Concurrently, she reports major depressive symptoms (persistent low mood, anhedonia, tearfulness, suicidal ideation) present for the majority of the illness course, satisfying Criterion C for schizoaffective disorder. Critically, she confirms a distinct period of ≥2 weeks where psychotic symptoms (paranoia, guardedness) persisted in the absence of depressive symptoms, fulfilling Criterion B (psychotic symptoms occurring without mood disturbance for a sustained period). No manic or hypomanic symptoms were endorsed, ruling out bipolar-type schizoaffective disorder or bipolar disorder with psychotic features. The overlap and integration of mood and psychotic symptoms across the majority of the illness, combined with the isolated psychotic-only period, is most consistent with Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type (F25.1) rather than Schizophrenia (which would not account for the prominent, majority-duration depressive syndrome) or Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (which would not account for the 2+ week period of psychosis without mood symptoms).
